content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text:
Sequential data combines ordered values and text. Prefer standard containers for ownership and bounds-aware interfaces where they fit the problem.

Views and String Views focuses on the decisions and observable behavior named by the subtopics below. The aim is to explain the rule, predict what a small program should do, and then confirm the result with a focused check.

Trace indexes from zero, distinguish element count from capacity, and check whether references or views can outlive or be invalidated by their source.

content_blocks.title: Minimal example: Views and String Views
content_blocks.run_instructions: Save as `example.cpp`. Compile using `g++ -std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic example.cpp -o example; then run ./example (Windows: .\example.exe).` The CodeLeaf page shows reference output only; it does not execute C++ learner code.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the example, rebuild with the same standard and warning flags, and rerun the same input. If the example is nondeterministic or depends on platform support, record that constraint instead of expecting byte-for-byte identical output.
content_blocks.limitations: The built-in CodeLeaf page does not execute C++ in a sandbox. Compile local teaching examples only; arbitrary learner code requires a separately deployed isolated runner with CPU, memory, process, filesystem and network limits.
content_blocks.explanation: string_view is non-owning: source must outlive every view that refers to it. Returning a view into a local string would dangle.

items.title: The Purpose of std::string_view (C++17)
items.text: std::string_view is a non-owning view of character data; the underlying storage must outlive every use of the view.

items.title: String Views Versus Owning Strings
items.text: Compare the alternatives in String Views Versus Owning Strings by their semantics, constraints and trade-offs; use the simpler option that satisfies the real requirement.

items.title: Avoiding Unnecessary String Copies
items.text: Explain avoiding unnecessary string copies in the context of Views and String Views: identify the rule, trace a minimal example, and check one boundary or failure case.

items.title: std::span (C++20)
items.text: std::span is a non-owning view over a contiguous sequence; it carries a size but does not own or extend the underlying storage lifetime.

items.text: Explain non-owning views of contiguous data in the context of Views and String Views: identify the rule, trace a minimal example, and check one boundary or failure case.
